jsonLd.description: Rosacea laser treatment is a Fotona Nd:YAG protocol that targets the vascular component of rosacea, reducing facial redness, visible vessels and flushing episodes as part of a long-term control plan.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin condition and there is no definitive cure. Nd:YAG laser controls the visible vascular component — redness, vessels and flushing — and reduces the visual impact of flares. Combined with trigger management and topical care, most patients achieve durable, meaningful improvement that is maintained with periodic sessions.

mainEntity.name: How many sessions will I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients complete three to five sessions spaced four to six weeks apart. The exact number depends on baseline severity, the density of visible vessels and how your skin responds to the first pass. We re-evaluate before each session with comparative photographs and only continue while documented improvement supports it.

Treated vessels do not return, but rosacea biology can produce new ones over time, especially when triggers persist. We typically recommend an annual maintenance session to address new vascular activity. Avoiding heat, alcohol, intense sun and stress, and following a barrier-supportive skincare routine, helps extend the result.
